narrative:
On August 18, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 43.3%, taking up 1,170 of the 2,701 scheduled matters across 52 judges. This reflects a continued upward trend in court-wide case clearance compared to recent proceedings, improving from 38.5% on August 13, 36.8% on August 14, and 41.5% on August 17.

Procedural and preliminary stages drove the bulk of the day's activity. The Orders category comprised the largest listing, converting 472 of 988 scheduled cases (47.8%), representing a clear efficiency gain over the 35.3% recorded on August 17. Admission matters converted at 44.6% (221 of 496). In contrast, substantive stages progressed more slowly; Final Hearing matters registered a 27.0% hearing rate (155 of 575), consistent with historical bottlenecks observed on August 14 (17.7%) and August 17 (25.7%), while Preliminary Hearings reached 35.9% (97 of 270).

Writ Petitions (WP) formed the largest caseload, with 443 of 1,091 matters heard (40.6%), rising from 35.5% the previous day. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) saw 224 of 467 cases heard (48.0%), while Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) moderated to 42.0% (131 of 312) from 56.2% on August 17. Regular Second Appeals (RSA) achieved high clearance at 70.2% (80 of 114), whereas Regular First Appeals (RFA) lagged at 29.7% (65 of 219).

Individual courtroom output varied significantly relative to cause-list size. Justice V. Srishananda achieved robust clearance, hearing 70 of 102 cases (68.6%), alongside Justice E.S. Indiresh (52 of 77, 67.5%) and Justice M. Nagaprasanna (73 of 140, 52.1%). Conversely, Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty managed the heaviest single docket, hearing 89 of 330 scheduled matters (27.0%).
